title: Grateful Dead Live at Recreation Hall, UC Davis on 1982-03-14
lineage: Master Soundboard Cassette > Reel to Reel > DAT > CDR

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard captures a hot ’82 show with scorching Let It Grow and seamless Scarlet→Fire transitions.
ai_review.review: The recording is a well‑balanced soundboard tape that most listeners describe as crystal clear, with only a faint background hiss. Musically the concert is high‑energy – the second set shines with tight, fiery runs from “Let It Grow” into a flawless “Scarlet > Fire”, plus memorable moments like Phil’s bass bombs on “Sugar Magnolia” and Brent’s standout keyboard solo. Overall the performance feels hot and tight, making this a must‑listen for 1982 Dead fans.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for both the musical performance (energy, standout songs) and the recording quality (clear, balanced soundboard), with only minor mixed remarks.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with well‑defined bass, drums and Brent's keys; a slight background hiss is noted by some listeners but does not detract from overall fidelity.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second‑set transitions are praised as seamless and exciting, especially Playin→Scarlet→Fire; the first set is described as solid with a strong opening of “One More Saturday Night”.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar tone clean and dynamic; vocal delivery praised though an early vocal entry on Scarlet was noted.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass bombs highlighted on Sugar Magnolia; generally tight, solid playing with a slight suggestion to boost bass presence in the mix.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s keyboard work shines – fresh tones, unique solo that many reviewers cite as a highlight of this era.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drums and cymbals well defined, especially during Let It Grow; overall tight rhythm section.
